arjun: Heads-up — while drafting SOC2 evidence I noticed /docs/security/audit-logs.md has a misleading SQL example. It only selects actor_id so service principals look identical to users. Also the Rust SDK snippet link 404s after we moved examples.
maria: Thanks. I'll change the SQL to explicitly include actor.type and show two sample rows (one user, one service_principal) so auditors can see the distinction. Plan: `SELECT ts, actor_id, actor.type, action FROM audit_events WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 days' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 10;` and add sample JSON.
sophie: Also rephrase the retention sentence. Current text "we retain logs for 90 days" sounds absolute. Recommend: "Default audit log retention is 90 days; enterprise contracts may specify different retention periods".
arjun: Great. Maria, can you also add a one-line note in docs/migration/audit-log-migration.md that queries depending on actor_id semantics may need actor.type filters post-migration?
maria: Yep. Opening PR now and running linkcheck.
docs-bot: Build started for PR (maria) 4bb 528.
maria: Linkcheck failed on one anchor in the migration doc. Fixing.
docs-bot: CI passed for PR (maria) :white_check_mark:.
sophie: Quick review done, left a tiny wording nit. LGTM after that.
maria: Addressed nit, squashed, merged. Deployed to staging and verified sample query returns correct actor.type rows.
arjun: I'll add the PR link to the SOC2 evidence tracker and attach the sample output snapshot. Thanks team.
sophie: Filing docs task to add automated smoke tests for example repo links so linkcheck will catch moved snippets earlier.
